subagent_run: 2026-06-10 (parent, #086 generation-fidelity sweep): the sweep's capture campaign aborted on a movement.ts-vs-engine collision divergence; investigated the engine's actual forward-step collision law.
tool: Ghidra headless (dump_function.py, fixed for pyghidra 3.x) on wmaze.ovr + dosbox-pure live oracle (trace-maze.ts collmap/collcells/wallplanes/stepprobe/recdump): BFS the real engine free-roam graph, read live DGROUP party fields + maze-record wall planes, compare to our static decode.
summary: movement.ts gates a forward step with isSolid(forwardEdge) (the RENDER-classify forward edge: wall code != 0 blocks). The ENGINE gates with a DIFFERENT, richer predicate: maze_can_step_in_facing (wmaze 0x3244) = maze_check_wall_in_direction (0xf2a, the wall-code read) + maze_can_pass_doors_and_walls (0x309d, a multi-condition target-cell/door/special4 gate). MEASURED on 120 engine-ground-truth (gx,gy,facing) views (collmap): movement.ts disagrees with the engine on 44/120 (37%) of forward steps OUTSIDE region 0 (it is byte-exact for the region-0 entrance cluster, which is why the renderer/MVP never caught it). The disagreement runs BOTH ways: 13 cells our model calls OPEN the engine BLOCKS, and 31 cells our model calls BLOCKED (wall code >= 2) the engine OPENS (e.g. gx128 gy121 facing1 has west wall code 2 yet the engine steps east through it -- confirmed by a clean live drive, not just BFS). PROVEN NOT the cause: (a) our wall DECODE is byte-perfect -- the live north(+0x60)/west(+0x120) 2-bit planes equal our static block for all 768 cells, no runtime mutation; (b) our resolve(gx,gy)->(region,cellA,cellB) is byte-perfect vs the engine's live z/x/y for all 140 sampled views; (c) region OVERLAP -- every explored cell is covered by exactly ONE region's 8x8 window, so resolution is unambiguous. CONCLUSION: passability is NOT a function of the forward wall code (no single wall-code threshold/rotation beats 33/120 errors; no single target-plane predicate beats 6 errors). It is the maze_can_pass_doors_and_walls multi-condition gate reading TARGET-cell passability planes (the getBits reads at 0x316b/0x317b/+0x49a) + a special4 in {1,2} && orient2==facing decoration block + door handling + game-state conditions. The exact predicate is NOT yet cracked (the 0x309d decompile is cdecl16-stack-arg-mangled; the plane offsets/widths it reads are not pinned).

engine_coordinate_law.region_window: maze_facing_covers_xy (0x357a): region r covers the global 8x8 window [gxBase[r]..gxBase[r]+7] x [gyBase[r]..gyBase[r]+7]. gxBase table @ record+0x1e0, gyBase @ record+0x1ec (12 bytes each).
engine_coordinate_law.resolve: maze_resolve_xy_to_facing (0x35b7): searches regions from the CURRENT region, then last-used (0x4fa6), then (cur+1)%12 onward; returns the first region whose window contains (gx,gy); blocks (returns 1) if none. Start-dependent IF windows overlap (none do in level 0).
engine_coordinate_law.cell_index: wall plane index = region*0x40 + cellA*8 + cellB, where cellA(=engine x @0x4f9e) = gy - gyBase[region], cellB(=engine y @0x4fa0) = gx - gxBase[region]. Verified identical to our resolve() + field() index.
engine_coordinate_law.facing_to_axis: VERIFIED live: facing 0 = +gy (gy+1), facing 1 = +gx (gx+1), facing 2 = -gy, facing 3 = -gx (maze_step_global_xy 0x108b: dir{0:y+=n,1:x+=n,2:y-=n,3:x-=n}).

findings.claim: The engine's forward-step collision is maze_can_step_in_facing (wmaze 0x3244), NOT the render-classify forward-edge that movement.ts reuses. 0x3244: iVar1 = maze_check_wall_in_direction(facing,z,y,x,gx,gy); if (iVar1 < 2) return maze_can_pass_doors_and_walls(facing, mode, iVar1); else return 1. maze_check_wall_in_direction (0xf2a): facing 0 -> north plane@+0x60 of CURRENT cell; facing 1 -> west plane@+0x120 of CURRENT cell; facing 2 -> maze_check_wall_north_step (0x36dd, 1 cell north, special handling for zones 10/12); facing 3 -> maze_check_wall_west_step (0x3742, 1 cell west).

evidence.details: dump_function.py wmaze 0x3244/0xf2a/0x309d/0x108b/0x35b7/0x357a. The wall-code branch (code>=2 -> return 1) does NOT match observed passability: gx128 gy121 facing1 has live west=2 but the engine steps east (clean stepprobe drive). So either the return-1 semantics are can-step (not blocked) for code>=2 -- contradicted by 20 code>=2 BLOCKED cases -- or maze_check_wall_in_direction returns a value other than the raw code. UNRESOLVED; the dominant gate is maze_can_pass_doors_and_walls.

findings.claim: movement.ts (isSolid(forwardEdge)) agrees with the engine for the region-0 entrance cluster but diverges on 44/120 (37%) forward steps once the party reaches regions 1/2/3. 13 our-OPEN/engine-BLOCKED (over-permissive -> breaks the navigation BFS used by the sweep capture harness), 31 our-BLOCKED/engine-OPEN (over-strict -> misses reachable cells). This is the root cause of the #086 sweep capture aborts (path divergence at gx123 gy123 facing0: our forwardEdge N(123,123)=0 says open, the engine blocks).

evidence.details: trace-maze.ts collmap (120 views, model-independent BFS over the engine graph) + stepprobe clean confirmations: (123,123,f0) N=0 -> engine BLOCKED; (128,122,f0) N=0 -> BLOCKED; (128,121,f1) W=2 -> engine OPEN (moved to 129,121); (127,121,f0) N=0 -> OPEN. Confusion table by forwardEdge code: code0 54open/13blocked, code1 0/2, code2 29open/16blocked, code3 2/4. No wall-code threshold beats 33 errors.

findings.claim: Our maze-block decode and resolve() are byte-exact vs the live engine; the collision divergence is NOT a decode/resolve bug. Live north(+0x60)/west(+0x120) 2-bit planes == our static block for all 768 cells (0 mismatches), stable across states (no runtime wall mutation; record @ DGROUP+0x7504). Engine resolved (region,x,y) == our (region,cellA,cellB) for all 140 sampled views.

evidence.details: trace-maze.ts wallplanes + collcells. cellA = gy-gyBase, cellB = gx-gxBase (gy-major); index region*64+cellA*8+cellB matches both the engine read and our field().

instruction_level_0x309d.note: ndisasm of wmaze.ovr (file offset == Ghidra image offset, anchored on maze_step_global_xy 0x108b). The block logic AFTER the wall-code branch:
instruction_level_0x309d.current_decoration_block: 0x309d-0x30ff: si = region*0x40 + cellA*8 + cellB (CURRENT cell). e3c1(base=record+0x1f8 special4, cell=si, width=4); if in {1,2}: e3c1(base=record+0x378 orient2, cell=si, width=2); if == facing([bp+4]) -> return 1 (BLOCKED). [special4 in {1,2} && orient2==facing blocks -- same orient2==facing gate as decoration rendering.]
instruction_level_0x309d.target_resolve_then_block: 0x3100-0x31a0: save gx/gy; maze_step_global_xy(facing) advances to target; maze_resolve_xy_to_facing on target. If UNRESOLVED -> restore + return 1 (BLOCKED). Else recompute si=target cell index, then: (A) e34b(param_1=[bp+6], si); if ==1 -> BLOCKED. (B) e34b(0x4e08, si); if ==1 -> BLOCKED; else continue toward pass. THEN reads e34b(record+0x43a pit, si) -> [bp-2] and e34b(record+0x49a, si) (used in the continue/door path, not the block).
instruction_level_0x309d.e34b: a 1-bit plane reader getBit(planeBase, cell) (confirmed: it reads the 1-bit pit plane record+0x43a the same way). e3c1 is the width-parameterized reader (2/4 bit) for north/west/special4/orient2.
instruction_level_0x309d.CAVEAT_wrong_function_risk: maze_can_step_in_facing (0x3244) has its ONLY callers inside maze_rotate_party (0x3304: 5 call sites 0x3401/3432/3463/3492/34b2). Each passes param_1 = &[bp-0x6a] (a LOCAL stack buffer, NOT a static plane) and on success calls maze_animate_temp_step (0x3286 = save-position/render/RESTORE preview). So 0x3244 may be an AUTO-STEP / TURN-PREVIEW path, NOT the UP-key forward-movement gate. param_1 being a local buffer means e34b(param_1,target) reads caller-prepared per-cell data, not a fixed plane. The UP-key forward gate must be confirmed by a LIVE INSTRUCTION TRACE before trusting this predicate.

windowed_tracer_2026-06-10.but_gate_not_isolated: Diffing OPEN vs BLOCKED to find the gate branch is defeated by stacked confounds: (a) single-pair diff is swamped by cell-data divergence -- the rarest divergent branch (res+0x25fa) disassembles to PRINTF number-formatting (different displayed coords), not collision; (b) the timer IRQ (handler at res~0x19xx) inserts random successors -- filtered by dropping that range; (c) FACING-dependence -- the collision code path differs by facing, so mixed-facing classes give 0 consistent branches; (d) even facing-0-only classes give 0 class-discriminating branches -- because post-gate paths diverge (some open moves cross a region + disk-LOAD, others don't) AND/OR the gate resides OUTSIDE the traced resident range [0x1a80,0x4784) (in another wroot code segment or an overlay called from resident).

watchpoint_instrumentation_2026-06-10.findings: (1) The move reads NOTHING from the static maze-record wall planes (recOff+0x60..+0x1e0) during a forward UP — collision doesn't read the raw record. (2) BLOCKED move runs ~0 code beyond idle (the press is nearly a no-op). (3) A differential read-watch (BLOCKED vs OPEN move, find addrs read by the same cs:ip with differing values) surfaced DGROUP ~0x68xx reads — BUT disasm proved these are STACK LOCALS (0x2c67 = `mov ax,[bp-0x4]`, 0x2c6f = `[bp-0xe]`); the STACK sits in DGROUP ~0x68xx, so the differential caught loop-counter/local differences in a party-status loop (imul 0x1b0 = party stride), NOT collision flags. (4) The flag 0x6894 is written by view_draw_sprite_at_depth (a render fn) — a render-state byte, not the move gate.
watchpoint_instrumentation_2026-06-10.wall: STACK POLLUTION + RENDER ENTANGLEMENT: the CPU stack occupies the same DGROUP region as any candidate flag area, so differential watchpoints are swamped by stack-local differences; and the move reads neither the record nor an isolable flag (collision appears enforced via the per-frame render-classify, shared state). Cracking the exact law would need to exclude the stack (find SS, watch only non-stack regions) AND disentangle from the render classify — i.e. it reduces to cracking the render's wall-classify pass itself (the long-open #077/#084-class decompiler-resistant classify at wmaze 0x39ec/0x3931/0x3946/0x3951).

ROOT_OBSERVABILITY_WALL_2026-06-10: gatestream (capture the ORDERED stream of the single OPEN frame that commits, idle-subtract): the move COMMITTED AT FRAME 0 and ran ONLY code already in the idle set (move-only = 0 distinct). DEFINITIVE EXPLANATION of every failed approach: the collision/availability check runs EVERY FRAME (idle included) to draw the on-screen movement-arrow widget (which directions are available); the keypress merely COMMITS the already-computed verdict (via a block-copy invisible to wwatch). Consequences: (a) idle-subtraction yields nothing (the collision code runs in idle too); (b) the named collision fns 0x3244/0x309d don't run in free-roam (a different per-frame availability computation does); (c) ANY two states compared (open vs blocked cell, adjacent or not) ALSO differ in per-frame RENDER, so the small availability branch is buried in render divergence; (d) successor/class/LCP diffs all drown in render + capture-timing noise. This is an OBSERVABILITY limit of differential range-tracing on the dosbox-pure harness, NOT code complexity. To crack faithfully would need a DATA WATCHPOINT (read-watch) on the per-direction availability flags with a backtrace to the computing instruction, or a single-step disassembling debugger to walk the per-frame check — neither in the current harness. PRAGMATIC: the ground-truth-validated collmap oracle (33/35) provides the collision verdict per (cell,facing) WITHOUT cracking the gate — sufficient for the #086 sweep navigation.
CONCLUSION_2026-06-10: After 6 approaches (static disasm, wwatch coord, candidate-fn trace, wwatch val-search, CS:IP sampling, data-driven fit): (1) the collision divergence is REAL + validated (33/35); (2) the real gate is in wroot-RESIDENT code (cs=0x1a8), NOT the wmaze maze_can_step/maze_can_pass functions (0 trace hits on a real move); (3) passability is NOT a static-cell-feature function (data-fit fails) -> likely dynamic state; (4) every current-harness tool hit a wall isolating the brief gate (single-point trace, render/IO-biased sampling, block-copy-blind wwatch). Cracking it faithfully needs NEW core instrumentation (a windowed/range instruction tracer to log the wroot-resident gate's reads+branch over an OPEN vs BLOCKED frame, OR a block-copy write hook) + RE of the wroot-resident handler -- a major sub-project. The collmap engine-oracle (now ground-truth-validated 33/35) already provides reliable model-independent navigation for the #086 sweep, sidestepping the crack.
